input.summary: Read the live branch PROGRESS.json (blob b3c23c40, 63 lines) and PR #226. PR #226 is open, head_sha 60b4d6cc, base main c30c23be, mergeable true. New finding from those two reads: PROGRESS.json on the branch is NOT the version I wrote (my write blob was 4b8c54ff per run 42555771004); it is the build-regenerated copy produced by the workflow's own commit step at head 60b4d6cc. So editing PROGRESS.json to force a fresh push run would be overwritten by the build step, creating another self-commit and moving the head again - the same trap. The forced push must therefore land on a path that is inside the workflow's path filter but never regenerated by the build: tests/test_repo_requirements_audit.py (or the workflow file itself). Both are in allowed_paths and in the workflow's push paths, and neither is written by build_matrices.py. Next I need the test file's blob sha and an exact anchor string before editing it.
input.next: Use the returned test-file text and blob sha to add one workflow-contract test via edit_file on tests/test_repo_requirements_audit.py: assert .github/workflows/venice-repo-requirements-audit.yml exists, triggers only on venice/repo-requirements-audit-v1, and contains the `git diff --cached --quiet` guard. That push is inside the workflow path filter and is never regenerated, so the run's commit step should find no diff and the head stays at my commit.

contribution.description: docs/venice-audit-v1/PROGRESS.json is build output, not authored state: my write landed as blob 4b8c54ff (run 42555771004) but the head 60b4d6cc replaced it with b3c23c40. Any attempt to force a fresh push run by editing PROGRESS.json would be overwritten by build_matrices.py, re-firing the guarded commit and moving the head again. The forced run must come from tests/test_repo_requirements_audit.py or the workflow file, which are in the push path filter and never regenerated.

pitfalls.problem: build_gantt.py opened with a single-quoted multi-line string, so importing it from build_matrices.py raised SyntaxError and the 'Build matrices from authority files' step exited 1 (run 42553625095).
pitfalls.failed_approach: Trusting the write_file ok=true receipt as proof the Python source parses; the receipt proves the blob landed, not that it is valid Python.
pitfalls.lesson: A new module imported by build_matrices must start with a real docstring or comment, and its first proof is the build step conclusion on the following push run - not the write receipt.
pitfalls.resolution: Docstring edit at 96ef7894 produced green run 42554257008.

pitfalls.problem: 'Commit regenerated matrices' exited 1 at 42553597443, which I initially attributed to an unguarded commit on a clean tree.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Diagnosing the failing step from its name instead of reading the step body; the workflow at 3fc6c647 already wraps commit/push in an `if git diff --cached --quiet` guard.
pitfalls.lesson: Read the workflow step body before proposing a workflow repair. When the guard is already present, a step-7 exit 1 means the else-branch ran and the commit or push itself failed, so look at tree state and remote head at that commit rather than rewriting the guard.
pitfalls.correction: Misdiagnosis corrected; no workflow change required for this id.

pitfalls.problem: Unauthenticated job pages return 'This step has been truncated due to its large size' for every step, so the failing log line is never visible.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Trying to read the cause from the job HTML page.
pitfalls.lesson: Use run_jobs step conclusions plus the annotation list (which names the step and 'Process completed with exit code 1'); never quote a log line that was not actually returned.

pitfalls.problem: The workflow's own 'Commit regenerated matrices' step pushes a commit, so the branch head no longer matches the sha the proven check-run covers. It pushed 187168f5 earlier and 60b4d6cc after run 42556696754, while that run's check-run head_sha stayed e3eba97e.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Treating a green run on the branch as sufficient for the merge gate, or assuming branch_head stays at the last file I wrote.
pitfalls.lesson: Before merge_pr, take branch_head and the branch run list in the same turn and match run.sha to the exact head. A green run whose sha is an ancestor does not authorize the merge.

pitfalls.problem: Head 60b4d6cc, created by the workflow's own commit step, has no workflow run in the branch run list, so the exact-head check requirement can never be met by polling.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Polling branch_head plus runs repeatedly and waiting for a run whose sha equals the self-commit head.
pitfalls.lesson: A commit pushed by a workflow step with the default GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger a new workflow run. To get a check at a stable head, push one allowed-path change yourself; once generated outputs are already committed the run's guarded commit step produces no diff and the head stays put.

pitfalls.problem: PROGRESS.json under docs/venice-audit-v1/ is rewritten by the build step, so authored text there does not survive and editing it re-fires the guarded commit.
